Hi Kimberly,

Quick background: Helio is closing its acquisition of Pulse Labs next month and legal wants the two existing Redwood private offers consolidated under the Helio master account. We have upcoming marketplace renewal windows for both AWS and GCP (Sept 30 acceptance deadline). Procurement asked me to confirm how Redwood wants us to handle:

- split POs vs single combined PO
- acceptance sequencing across AWS/GCP
- any required DocuSign flows for private offers

Can you advise who we should loop in on the Redwood side to get the correct private-offer IDs and a recommended billing path? We're trying to avoid duplicate invoices during the first quarter post-close.

Attachments: none in this message.

Thanks,
Marta Ruiz
Head of Procurement, Helio Health

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Marketplace renewal & account merger — next steps

Marta — thanks for the heads up and congrats on the close. Short answer: we can consolidate, but there are operational steps to avoid billing gaps. Proposed immediate plan:

1) You send a single combined PO for the first renewal period with a note splitting committed capacity by legacy account (Helio vs Pulse) so we can map consumption in billing reconciliation.

2) Redwood will request explicit private-offer ID transfers on each marketplace. For AWS/GCP we need both the private-offer IDs and the buyer account IDs. Jordan and Marcus are the leads for marketplace paperwork; they will identify the precise acceptance path (single accept vs staged).

3) DocuSign: we typically generate separate DocuSign envelopes per marketplace/private-offer because each provider requires their own acceptance record. We can coordinate envelope links to be sent to Procurement once we have the PO and account IDs.

Next steps on our side: Jordan, Marcus — can you confirm the acceptance windows that allow a staged acceptance (Pulse first, Helio final) vs single-sweep acceptance, and whether there are any e-billing caveats if the buyer account ids change post-acceptance?

Thanks — attaching a short acceptance checklist (I'll upload the template once Jordan confirms).

Best,
Kimberly Park
Director, Marketplace & Renewals
Redwood Inference

Marta / team — quick technical notes from the marketplace side: 

- AWS: private offers can be accepted by a single buyer account. If you want consumption consolidated under the Helio master, the safest path is to accept from the Helio buyer account and migrate usage from Pulse via tagging for one billing quarter. If Pulse needs to accept first for legal reasons, we can do a staged acceptance but you'll see two invoice streams for that quarter.

- GCP: we can map commitments to a consolidated billing account but GCP's reseller flow will require we close the transfer window before the acceptance deadline; otherwise you risk losing the private-offer pricing.

Requested from Helio: buyer account IDs for both the Helio master and the Pulse legacy account, and a combined PO (PDF). Once we have that we will:
  * Create acceptance envelopes per marketplace (DocuSign links to follow)
  * Open a short ticket with the marketplace AMs to flag the cross-account consolidation so they avoid double charging the first billing cycle

Marcus — can you check tax/VAT line items if Helio is migrating billing between accounts in different sub-entities? Priyom — please prepare a short memo on the billing cutover risks to share with Helio procurement.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Marketplace Partnerships
Redwood Inference

1) We'll proceed with single acceptance from the Helio master account for both AWS and GCP.
2) Redwood will generate two DocuSign envelopes (one per marketplace). Expect DocuSign links to arrive by 2028-08-02. The envelopes will include a short addendum noting the Pulse acknowledgement PDF can be attached as evidence (does not need to be a marketplace acceptance).

4) Priyom is drafting a one-page risk memo on invoice fallthrough/tax treatment and will share by 2028-07-28.

Action items for Helio: please upload the Pulse acknowledgement PDF to the DocuSign envelope when you receive it, and confirm your legal signatory for the DocuSign envelopes (name & email) so I can pre-fill the recipients.

I'll open the marketplace ticket and ping AWS/GCP AMs today to flag the cross-account consolidation.
